display.purpose: Headings, window title-bar captions, badge-scale chrome labels only — never body copy.

body.purpose: All read content: bio, descriptions, data readouts, nav labels.

motion.name: bevel-press
motion.purpose: Button hover/active bevel and translate steps — deliberately steppy, never eased smooth.

motion.name: rail-glide
motion.purpose: Commit-rail active indicator repositioning; plain CSS transition, not the View Transitions API (see DESIGN.md Do's and Don'ts).

motion.name: glitch-split
motion.purpose: One-frame RGB misregistration pulse on hover/focus, donated from the declined riso-misregistration challenger.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The hero's 'RUN projects.exe' call to action.
components.css: .ds-pixel-btn { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Silkscreen', monospace; border: 2px solid #05060a; background: #0f3320; color: #3dff77; padding: 12px 20px; border-radius: 0; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #3dff77, inset -2px -2px 0 #020305; transition: background 80ms steps(2), color 80ms steps(2); } .ds-pixel-btn:hover, .ds-pixel-btn:focus-visible { background: #3dff77; color: #0a0c12; }

components.name: Window
components.description: The system's signature container: a bordered, beveled OS window with a title bar, used for every content section.
components.css: .ds-window { border: 2px solid #05060a; background: #12151f; box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 #3a4160, inset -1px -1px 0 #020305; } .ds-window-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border-bottom: 2px solid #05060a; background: #05060a; padding: 8px 12px; } .ds-window-corner { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: #1f9a4d; } .ds-window-corner--alt { background: #2a6b3f; } .ds-window-title { font-family: 'Silkscreen', monospace; font-size: 11px; color: #8b93ac; } .ds-window-body { padding: 24px; color: #e9ecdf; font-family: 'VT323', monospace; font-size: 18px; }

components.name: Verdict Badge
components.description: Repo classification chip; color is always traceable to the repo's real GitHub topics.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-block; border: 1px solid; padding: 2px 8px; font-family: 'VT323', monospace; font-size: 14px; border-radius: 0; } .ds-badge--open { color: #5be07f; border-color: #2a6b3f; } .ds-badge--coursework { color: #ffbd4f; border-color: #7a5a1f; } .ds-badge--hackathon { color: #ff7ad1; border-color: #7a3562; } .ds-badge--research { color: #6f9dff; border-color: #2f4a7a; }

components.name: Commit Rail Node
components.description: One section node on the desktop-only left navigation rail, rendered as a git-graph.
components.css: .ds-rail-node { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 0 8px 20px; text-decoration: none; } .ds-rail-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border: 1px solid #3a4160; background: #05060a; } .ds-rail-node--active .ds-rail-dot { border-color: #3dff77; background: #3dff77; } .ds-rail-label { font-family: 'VT323', monospace; font-size: 18px; color: #737d9c; } .ds-rail-node--active .ds-rail-label { color: #3dff77; }

narrative.overview: The site does not decorate itself with pixel motifs — it renders as an actual 16-color computer that has just powered on. Every surface lives inside a bordered, beveled 'window' docked to a fixed region, the way a PC-98-era or early-Windows desktop composes itself from chrome, not cards. The system replaces the incumbent look entirely; that look is anti-reference only, kept nowhere in the new build. Two donated disciplines keep the world from reading as a costume: the site's own navigation is a literal git commit graph, and repo badges borrow judge-verdict coloring from competitive-programming scoreboards rather than an arbitrary tag palette. A third donation — a one-frame RGB channel misregistration pulse on hover/focus, lifted from risograph print misalignment — is the system's only 'glitch' and it never runs continuously.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed 24px pixel grid as the page's literal material, not a decorative afterthought
Hard 2-tone bevel borders (inset/outset) stand in for all depth — no soft shadows anywhere
Two bitmap/CRT-lineage faces only: Silkscreen for display, VT323 for everything read at length
Live GitHub data rendered as terminal-style readouts, never restyled as generic stat cards
Repo preview images are ordered-dithered to the locked palette on canvas at load time

rules.name: The Verdict Rule
rules.body: Color on a badge or status dot always means a classification a visitor could look up, never a mood or a decorative accent.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page is set in a third font. A word is either a computer's own label (Silkscreen) or content a person wrote (VT323).

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every depth cue is a hard 1px bevel pair. A soft or colored glow shadow never ships.

dos: Do keep every badge color traceable to the repo's actual GitHub topics/visibility.
Do dither any new photographic or screenshot imagery through the same ordered Bayer 4×4 pass at the locked duotone, with a plain-img fallback for CORS failures.
Do keep every text token at or above 4.5:1 contrast against its background.
donts: Don't call document.startViewTransition from a scroll/IntersectionObserver callback in this codebase — it reliably corrupted the page's paint near hydration in testing.
Don't introduce a soft or colored box-shadow anywhere.
